summary: Alfred Forke was a scholar of sinology and philosophy who studied at the University of Geneva and the University of Berlin. He held posts at the Seminar für Orientalische Sprachen zu Berlin, the University of Berlin, and the University of Hamburg.

Alfred Foucher worked in Indology, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at the École Normale Supérieure and under Sylvain Lévi at the EPHE, he held positions at EFEO, EPHE, the University of Paris, and the Délégation Archéologique Française en Afghanistan.

Alfred Gell studied at Cambridge under Edmund Leach and completed his Ph.D. at the London School of Economics. He subsequently held academic posts at the University of Sussex, the Australian National University, and the London School of Economics.

Alfred Hillebrandt was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler at the University of Breslau and Martin Haug at the University of Munich. He held a professorship and chair at the University of Breslau from 1883 to 1921.
Alfred Körte specialized in archaeology and linguistics, studying at the University of Bonn. His career included posts at the universities of Bonn, Greifswald, Basel, Giessen, Freiburg, and Leipzig.

Indologist and linguist Alfred Ludwig studied at the University of Vienna and the University of Berlin under Albrecht Weber, Hermann Bonitz, Anton Boller, and others. He habilitated at Vienna in 1858 and served as a professor at the University of Prague.

Alfred Radcliffe-Brown studied at the University of Cambridge and Trinity College, Cambridge. He held academic posts at the University of Sydney, the University of Chicago, the University of Oxford, and the Fundação Escola de Sociologia e Política de São Paulo.
Ali Asani works in religious studies and Indology. He holds a post at Harvard University and serves on the editorial board of Perspectives on Islamicate South Asia.

Linguist Alice Harris studied at Harvard University and the University of Massachusetts Amherst. She held posts at Vanderbilt University from around 1979 to 2002 and at the University of Massachusetts Amherst around 2009.

Alicia Turner works in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Chicago, studying under Bruce Lincoln, Steven Collins, Saw Tun, Daw Than Than Win, John Okell, and Carol S. Anderson.
Alison Denton Jones works in religious studies, sinology, and Buddhist studies. She studied under Martin King Whyte, Allan H. Barr, Mingfei Gao, and Margaret Dornish.

Alka Patel specializes in archaeology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She studied at Mount Holyoke College and earned her PhD from Harvard University, later serving as Associate Professor at the University of California, Irvine.

Allan G. Grapard was a scholar of Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. After earning a Ph.D. from INALCO, he held a professorship in Shinto Studies at the University of California, Santa Barbara from 1985 to 2010.

Allan Gibbard is a philosopher who studied at Swarthmore College and Harvard University. He held posts at the University of Chicago (1969–1974), the University of Pittsburgh (1974–1977), and the University of Michigan (1977–2016).
Allan H. Barr is a sinologist who completed his doctorate at the University of Oxford by 1983. He served as Professor of Asian Languages and Literatures at Pomona College.

Indologist Allen Wright Thrasher studied under doctoral supervisor Daniel H. H. Ingalls as well as traditional teachers Vighnahari Bhalacandra Deo, R. Srinivasan Raghavachariar, and K. A. Sivaramakrishna Sastri. He held a post at the Library of Congress.
Alnis Dickson specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed an MA at McGill University, studying under Lara Braitstein and G. Victor Sōgen Hori.

Alois Anton Führer studied Indology and archaeology at Würzburg under Julius Jolly and with Georg Bühler. He held posts at St. Xavier's College, the State Museum Lucknow, the Archaeological Survey of India, and later the Christian Catholic Church of Switzerland.
Alois Müller worked in linguistics and held posts at the Vienna University Library (~1865–1901), Palacký University Olomouc (1874–1879), and Graz University Library as director in 1879.

Aloys Sprenger studied at Vienna under Joseph von Hammer-Purgstall and Vinzenz Rosenzweig von Schwannau, and at Leiden. He headed Zakir Husain Delhi College, Hooghly Mohsin College, and Aliah University, later serving as professor at the University of Bern (1857–1881).
